findings.evidence: Lines 496–507 recurse on words but conclude membership in `filtration Q l.length`; after removing the head, every resulting term has degree at most the predecessor.
findings.fix: Expose a theorem sending `filtration Q (k + 1)` into `filtration Q k` (and handle `F₀` separately if useful), deriving the weaker preservation result from it.
findings.issue: `contractLeft_mem_filtration` only proves `Fₖ → Fₖ`, despite contraction canonically lowering positive filtration degree; consumers cannot use the advertised “shorter words” behavior.

findings.evidence: The only public exact characterization is `(filtration Q k).map (changeFormEquiv h).toLinearMap = filtration Q' k` at lines 543–551; grep finds no `changeFormEquiv` filtration membership lemma.
findings.fix: Add a `@[simp]` theorem stating `(changeFormEquiv h x ∈ filtration Q' k) ↔ x ∈ filtration Q k`; also mark the map equality `[simp]` if it has the intended normal-form orientation.
findings.issue: The exact transport theorem has no membership-iff restatement or simplification annotation, so routine goals about `(changeFormEquiv h) x ∈ filtration Q' k` require manually unpacking `Submodule.map`.

summary: The new surface under-specifies contraction’s degree behavior and lacks the normal-form membership API for the change-form equivalence.
